title: Command words: what each one wants
specPoints: OCR's command words (specification section 3d): state, identify, give, list, define, describe, explain, compare, discuss, evaluate, justify, outline, show, calculate, complete, write, refine, design, draw, annotate and others
The shape of answer each command word requires; matching the shape to the marks
learn: Recognise the command word in any question stem and underline it
Say what each common command word asks for, in OCR's sense
Produce the right *shape* of answer: a word, a sentence, a point-plus-reason, a balanced argument, code
Spot the three words that most often lose marks (describe vs explain; compare; discuss) and handle them
Rewrite a weak answer so it matches its command word
hook: 'State one advantage of SSDs.' 'Explain one advantage of SSDs.' Same topic, same mark scheme list — different marks. The first wants a fact. The second wants the fact *and why it matters*. Read the first word of the question before you read anything else.

video.title: Command words in 4 minutes
video.brief: Sort the command words into four columns on screen: Recall (state, identify, give, list, define, name) · Account (describe, outline) · Reasons (explain, justify) · Weigh up (compare, discuss, evaluate). Then the practical ones: write, complete, show, calculate, draw, design, refine. For each column show one stem and a one-line model answer, highlighting the part that earns the second mark. End with the three traps.

explain.code:
Recall — short, no reasons
  State / Give       a specific name, value or brief answer, no explanation
  Identify           pick out and state briefly, e.g. from a list or diagram
  List               a sequence of brief answers, no explanation
  Define             the precise meaning of the term

Account — say what it is or how it works
  Describe           a detailed account of a situation, process or feature (what / how)
  Outline            a brief account or summary

Reasons — say why
  Explain            a detailed account INCLUDING reasons or causes (what + why / because)
  Justify            valid reasons or evidence to support an answer or conclusion

Weigh up — more than one side
  Compare            similarities AND differences, referring to BOTH items throughout
  Discuss            a considered, balanced review with a range of arguments; conclusions supported
  Evaluate           assess implications and limitations; make a judgement against criteria

Do — produce something
  Write / Rewrite    produce code or an algorithm (Section B: ERL or a high-level language)
  Complete           fill in all the missing parts (table, code, diagram)
  Show               give the steps (a search, a sort, a calculation)
  Calculate          numerical answer WITH working
  Draw / Annotate    diagram / add brief notes to a diagram
  Design             produce a plan or model (natural English, pseudocode, flowchart allowed)
  Refine             improve, make more efficient, modify
after: These paraphrase OCR's published definitions; the exact wording is in the specification, section 3d.

list: **Describe treated as explain** (or the reverse). *Describe* = what it is / how it works. *Explain* = and **why** — the second mark is almost always after the word 'because' or 'so that'. If your explain answer has no 'because', it is a describe answer.

**Compare answered as two separate descriptions.** A compare needs sentences that hold both items at once: 'X does … **whereas** Y does …'. Two paragraphs, one on each, scores poorly even if every fact is right.
**Discuss answered as a list.** Discuss wants more than one side, developed, applied to the scenario, and a conclusion. Bullet points of advantages score low bands.

explain.code:
State one input device.                     Keyboard.
Describe one feature of an IDE.             Syntax highlighting shows keywords, strings and
                                            comments in different colours.
Explain one benefit of syntax highlighting. Syntax highlighting colours keywords and strings
                                            differently, SO THAT an unclosed string or misspelt
                                            keyword stands out and can be fixed quickly.
Compare RAM and ROM.                        RAM is volatile WHEREAS ROM keeps its contents
                                            without power; BOTH are primary storage; RAM holds
                                            running programs WHILE ROM holds the boot firmware.
Justify the use of a compiler here.         A compiler is appropriate BECAUSE the software is sold
                                            to customers, so a stand-alone executable that hides
                                            the source and runs fast is needed.

p: Underline the command word. Circle the number of marks. Box the scenario words you must use. Then answer. Thirty seconds, every question. It is the cheapest habit in the exam.

simple.h: The first word tells you the job
list: **State / Give / Identify / List**: a short fact. No reasons.
**Describe**: say what it is or how it works.
**Explain**: say what *and why* — use 'because' or 'so that'.
**Compare**: both things in the same sentence — 'X … whereas Y …'.
**Discuss / Evaluate**: both sides, applied to the situation, and your conclusion.
**Write / Complete / Show / Calculate**: do it, and show your steps.

p: Explain with no 'because' = half marks. Compare as two separate paragraphs = low marks. Discuss as a bullet list = low band.
Underline the command word. Circle the marks. Box the scenario words. Then write.

keyterms.def: The instruction word at the start of a question that says what kind of answer is wanted.
Give an account of what something is or how it works.
Give an account including reasons — what and why.
Give similarities and differences, referring to both items throughout.
Give a balanced review of several arguments and reach a supported conclusion.
Give valid reasons supporting an answer or decision.

try.title: 1. Sort the stems
p: Put each into Recall / Account / Reasons / Weigh up / Do: 'Identify the output of…' · 'Describe how a bubble sort works' · 'Explain why the program uses a constant' · 'Compare linear and binary search' · 'Justify the choice of data type' · 'Show the stages of a merge sort' · 'Discuss the impact of…' · 'Outline the role of the operating system' · 'Refine the algorithm so that…' · 'Define the term abstraction'.

try.title: 2. Upgrade the answer
p: Each answer is correct for a weaker command word. Rewrite it for the one asked. (a) *Explain one advantage of a mesh network.* Answer given: 'There is more than one route between devices.' (b) *Compare a compiler and an interpreter.* Answer given: 'A compiler translates all at once. An interpreter goes line by line.' (c) *Justify the use of a 2D array for a chessboard.* Answer given: 'A 2D array has rows and columns.'

try.title: 3. Spot the 'because'
p: Take the model answers in the exam sections of any three lessons in 2.1–2.5 that use *explain*. Underline the word that introduces the reason in each (because / so that / which means / as). Then write one explain answer of your own for a topic of your choice and underline yours.

try.title: 4. Stem surgery
p: Write the same question six ways — state, describe, explain, compare, justify, discuss — about **cloud storage**. For each, write the number of marks you'd expect and a one-line model answer of the right shape.

try.title: 5. Exam command-word practice
instructions: Use the answer builder to assemble explain and compare answers from parts, and see where the second mark comes from.

opts: Refer to both items throughout, with similarities and differences
A balanced range of arguments and a supported conclusion

check.q: 'Show the stages of a bubble sort' wants:

exam.q: **Describe** what is meant by a logic error.
model: An error in the design/logic of the program (1) so that it runs but produces an unexpected or incorrect result (1).
exam.commentary: Describe: what it is and what happens. No 'why' needed.

exam.q: **Explain** why a logic error is harder to find than a syntax error.
model: A syntax error stops the program and is reported with a line number, whereas a logic error produces no message (1) **because** the code is valid and runs, so the error only shows as wrong output that must be found by testing/tracing (1).
exam.commentary: Same topic, now with reasons. Notice the second mark lives after 'because'.

model: Both repeat a block of code (1). A for loop repeats a fixed, known number of times **whereas** a while loop repeats while a condition is true, an unknown number of times (1). A for loop uses a counter variable **while** a while loop needs the body to change the condition (1). A while loop may run zero times **but** a for loop with a valid range always runs (1).
exam.commentary: Every sentence names both loops. One similarity plus differences is the full-marks shape.

home: Make a one-page command-word card: the four groups, the key word in each (because / whereas / both sides), and one model sentence for each. Laminate it mentally — it goes on your desk for every practice paper from now on.

teacher.timing: 60 min: hook 3 · explain 14 · try 28 · check 5 · exam 7 · homework 3
misconceptions: Thinking 'justify' means 'describe the thing you chose'. It means give reasons for the choice *in this context*.
say: 'First word of the question. Circle it. Now what shape is the answer?'
teacher.skip: Try 5 optional. Try 2 is the one that moves grades.
differentiation: Support: Try 1 as a card sort with the four headings laid out.
Stretch: Try 4 at speed — six answers in six minutes.
teacher.examiner_review: Jose: definitions are paraphrased from the J277 specification section 3d (full list: add, analyse, annotate, calculate, compare, complete, convert, define, describe, design, discuss, draw, evaluate, explain, give, how, identify, justify, label, list, order, outline, refine, show, solve, state, tick, what, write/rewrite). Please check the 'describe = what, explain = what + why' framing matches how J277 schemes actually credit the second mark, and add any command word you see misread in scripts.
